In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of structure based drug discovery approaches to discover new small molecule inhibitors of important protein protein interactions.
the discovery of small molecule inhibitors to target p53-Mdm2 interaction and other protein protein interactions.
the discovery of small molecule PPIs inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the approaches described in the thesis are important contributions to the field of medicinal chemistry and drug discovery.
the work presented in this dissertation provides an important foundation and framework for the development of small molecule PPI modulators.
the methods developed in this dissertation have provided a new approach for the design of small molecules to target protein protein interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to generate novel scaffolds of PPI inhibitors by structure based drug design.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of a structure based drug discovery approach to target PPI inhibitors, which can be applied to other PPI targets.
we have developed a novel, efficient, and transformative strategy for the design, synthesis and evaluation of small molecule inhibitors targeting protein protein interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the discovery of novel PPI inhibitors can be achieved by the application of a combination of structural biology information and multicomponent reactions.

small molecule inhibitors of p53/Mdm-2 and other PPIs can be designed by combining structural insights, multicomponent reactions and ligand design, and that these compounds can serve as starting points for medicinal chemistry optimization.
the discovery of small molecules targeting PDI is not a pipe dream, but can be achieved by applying the approaches developed in this work.
